subject: Using the child()-command with several subfolders

messages.author: 9fc3760cd9d4deef
messages.subject: Using the child()-command with several subfolders
parts:
I have several subfolders with child-documents. Now, my code does not
run anymore (version 0.5.0) although I'm pretty sure it run before.
What do I miss?

My parent-document Test.Rnw, which lies in the main folder:

\documentclass[11pt]{article}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{document}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%% Sweave Options %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

<<Test1, child='Subfolder1/File1.Rnw', eval=TRUE>>=
@

<<Test2, child='Subfolder2/File2.Rnw', eval=TRUE>>=
@

\end{document}

Then I have two subfolders named "Subfolder1" and "Subfolder2", each
including one file ("File1.Rnw" and "File2.Rnw", respectively):

File1.Rnw:

\section{1}

Test

<<>>=
1 + 1
@

File2.Rnw:

\section{2}

Test

<<>>=
2 + 2
@

When I knit the Test.Rnw file, I get the following error:

Warning in file(con, "r") :
cannot open file './/Subfolder1//Subfolder2/File2.Rnw': No such file
or directory
label: Test2 (with options)
List of 2
$ child: chr "Subfolder2/File2.Rnw"
$ eval : logi TRUE

Error in process_file(text) :
Quitting from lines 9-9: Error in file(con, "r") : cannot open the
connection

So the problem seems to be that knitr is adding the subfolder of the
first chunk to the second chunk. I do not understand this and I have
not found any hint on the documentation why this is so. Any help would
be appreciated!

Platform: x86_64-pc-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)

locale:

LC_MONETARY=German_Germany.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C
LC_TIME=C
